topics.metaDescription: Cross-platform app development lets you ship to iOS and Android from one codebase — faster and more affordable than building twice. Here's how Auaha does it.
topics.intro: Building the same app twice — once for iOS, once for Android — is slow and expensive. Cross-platform development uses a single codebase to ship to both, which means lower cost, faster delivery, and a consistent experience.

checks.t: iOS and Android from the same source, instead of two separate builds and two bills.
Less duplicate work means a quicker path to launch and a lower budget.
Your app looks and behaves the same on every device, with one place to fix bugs and add features.

body: Auaha builds cross-platform apps with Flutter, a mature framework backed by Google that produces fast, natively-compiled apps for iOS and Android from one codebase. We pair it with reliable cloud backends for auth, data, and sync.
For the vast majority of apps, cross-platform is the right call. When a project genuinely needs platform-specific native work, we'll tell you that up front.

faqs.q: What is cross-platform app development?
faqs.a: It's building a single codebase that runs on both iOS and Android, rather than developing two separate native apps. It lowers cost, speeds up delivery, and keeps the experience consistent across devices.

faqs.q: Is cross-platform as good as native?
faqs.a: For most apps, yes — modern frameworks like Flutter produce fast, natively-compiled apps. Native still has its place for certain hardware-intensive or platform-specific needs, and we'll flag it when that applies to your project.

faqs.q: Does cross-platform save money?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. One codebase for both platforms means less duplicate development and a single place to maintain and improve the app.

topics.metaDescription: Auaha builds fast, cross-platform iOS and Android apps with Flutter — one codebase, native performance. Here's why Flutter and how we use it.
topics.intro: Flutter is a modern, Google-backed framework for building natively-compiled apps for iOS and Android from a single codebase. It's what Auaha builds with — and why we can ship polished apps to both platforms efficiently.

checks.t: Flutter compiles to native code, so apps are fast and smooth — not sluggish web wrappers.
iOS and Android from the same source, which keeps cost and timelines down.
Pixel-level control means your app looks the way it should on every device.
Backed by Google with a large ecosystem, so it's a safe long-term foundation.

faqs.q: What is Flutter?
faqs.a: Flutter is an open-source framework from Google for building natively-compiled mobile apps for iOS and Android from a single codebase. It's known for fast performance and precise, consistent UI.

faqs.q: Is Flutter good for production apps?
faqs.a: Yes — Flutter is used in production by companies large and small. Auaha has shipped real Flutter apps to the App Store.

faqs.q: Can Flutter apps use device features?
faqs.a: Yes — camera, location, notifications, secure storage, and more are all supported through Flutter's plugin ecosystem.

topics.metaDescription: Validate your idea without building the whole thing. Auaha builds lean MVPs for startups — the core of your app, shipped fast, so you can learn from real users.
topics.intro: You don't need to build everything to find out if an idea works. A minimum viable product ships the core of your app fast, so you can get it in front of real users, learn, and decide what to build next with evidence instead of guesses.

checks.t: We help you cut to the one or two things your app must do, and leave the rest for later.
Cross-platform build means a working iOS and Android app sooner and for less.
Get it in front of users, see what actually matters, and build the next version on real feedback.

faqs.q: What is an MVP?
faqs.a: A minimum viable product is the simplest version of your app that delivers real value — enough to put in front of users and learn from, without the cost and time of building every feature up front.

faqs.q: How long does an MVP take?
faqs.a: It depends on scope, but keeping an MVP focused on the core is exactly what makes it fast. We scope it with you so you know the timeline before we start.

faqs.q: Can you grow the MVP later?
faqs.a: Yes — a well-built MVP is the foundation for the full product. We build it to grow, then add features as your app proves itself.

topics.metaDescription: Auaha builds for iOS and Android together, from one codebase — so you launch on both the App Store and Google Play without paying to build twice.
topics.intro: Your users are on both iPhone and Android, so your app should be too. Auaha builds for both platforms from a single codebase, so you launch on the App Store and Google Play without doubling the budget.

body: Instead of hiring separate iOS and Android teams, a cross-platform build gives you both from one source. That means a consistent experience for every user and a single place to fix bugs and ship new features.
We handle the full path on each platform — build, store setup, and release — so getting onto the App Store and Google Play isn't something you have to figure out alone.

faqs.q: Can one app work on both iPhone and Android?
faqs.a: Yes — a cross-platform app is built from a single codebase that runs natively on both iOS and Android, so you reach every user without building two separate apps.

faqs.q: Do you handle App Store and Google Play submission?
faqs.a: Yes — we handle the build, store setup, and release process for both the Apple App Store and Google Play.

faqs.q: Will the app feel native on both?
faqs.a: Yes — we build with Flutter, which compiles to native code, so the app is fast and feels right on both platforms.
